name: BRAF Inhibitor +/- MEK Inhibitor (Histiocytic Neoplasm, BRAF V600E: dabrafenib/vemurafenib +/- trametinib/cobimetinib)
disease: Histiocytic neoplasm (Langerhans cell histiocytosis / Erdheim-Chester disease)
histology: histiocytic neoplasm - Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) or Erdheim-Chester disease (ECD), including multisystem, single-system lung, and CNS-involved disease

biomarkers.BRAF: V600E mutation - the biomarker gate for BRAF-inhibitor therapy (present in ~50% of LCH and >80% of ECD histiocytoses)
biomarkers.MAPK: for MAP-kinase-pathway (non-BRAF-V600E) mutations, or no actionable/detectable mutation, a MEK inhibitor (trametinib, binimetinib, or selumetinib) is the targeted option instead of a BRAF inhibitor
biomarkers.note: BRAF inhibitors (dabrafenib, vemurafenib) are used for BRAF V600E-mutated LCH and ECD, alone or combined with a MEK inhibitor (trametinib or cobimetinib). MEK inhibitors are used for MAP-kinase-pathway mutations or no detectable actionable mutation. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Histiocytic Neoplasms, HIST-F (Principles of Targeted Therapy) and the Discussion (MS-9, treatment of LCH/ECD).

treatmentSetting: targeted therapy for BRAF V600E-mutated histiocytic neoplasm (LCH/ECD)
lineOfTherapy: targeted option for BRAF V600E-mutated LCH or ECD (systemic therapy); continued long-term as disease control (relapse is common on discontinuation)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: BRAF V600E mutation confirmed (required for BRAF-inhibitor therapy)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, Discussion MS-9 (dabrafenib/vemurafenib for BRAF V600E-mutated LCH; vemurafenib/dabrafenib for BRAF V600E-mutated ECD); histiocytic lines 3428, 3623, 3627, 3631

drugs.name: Dabrafenib

provenance.locator: HIST-F (Principles of Targeted Therapy - Recommended Starting Doses for Select Targeted Agents): Dabrafenib 50 mg PO twice daily; histiocytic line 2730

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Histiocytic Neoplasms v2.2026, HIST-F table (line 2730): Dabrafenib 50 mg PO TWICE daily as the recommended STARTING dose (adjust/increase based on response). dosePerUnit 50 mg is the single per-administration dose given BID; represented as days 1 to 28 continuously. This is a reduced histiocytic starting dose (below the melanoma label dose); it is generally reasonable to start with one or two dose reductions and titrate to response (HIST-F, Considerations for Targeted Therapies). ALTERNATIVE BRAF INHIBITOR: vemurafenib 480 mg PO twice daily (HIST-F, line 2736). No ISMP tall-man form.

drugs.name: Trametinib

provenance.locator: HIST-F (Principles of Targeted Therapy): Trametinib 0.5-1 mg PO daily; histiocytic line 2734

drugs.notes: OPTIONAL MEK-INHIBITOR PARTNER (the '+/- MEKi'). Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Histiocytic Neoplasms v2.2026, HIST-F (line 2734): Trametinib recommended STARTING dose 0.5 to 1 mg PO once daily (adjust/increase based on response). Modeled at the 1 mg upper end of the starting range; the source range is 0.5-1 mg and it is titrated to response. Trametinib may also be used as single-agent MEK-inhibitor therapy for MAP-kinase-pathway mutations or no detectable actionable mutation. ALTERNATIVE MEK INHIBITOR: cobimetinib 20-40 mg PO daily on days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle (HIST-F, line 2732); binimetinib or selumetinib if cobimetinib/trametinib not tolerated. If a BRAF inhibitor is given WITHOUT a MEK inhibitor, this drug is omitted. No ISMP tall-man form.

supportiveCare: Continuous oral dosing (no defined cycle count); targeted therapy is continued long-term because histiocytic disease commonly relapses on discontinuation. Start at reduced doses and titrate to response per HIST-F.

BRAF inhibitor: dabrafenib 50 mg PO twice daily OR vemurafenib 480 mg PO twice daily. Optional MEK inhibitor: trametinib 0.5-1 mg PO daily OR cobimetinib 20-40 mg PO daily on days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle.

MEK inhibitor: serious retinopathy can occur - baseline and periodic retinal exam with optical coherence tomography (OCT); acneiform rash managed with topical benzoyl peroxide +/- oral doxycycline/minocycline.
BRAF inhibitor after prior immune checkpoint blockade: drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome can occur - prompt dermatology consultation.

monitoring: MEK-inhibitor retinopathy: retinal exam with OCT (baseline and periodic)
cutaneous toxicity (BRAFi: keratoacanthoma/squamous proliferations, hypersensitivity; MEKi: acneiform rash)
cardiac (MEK-inhibitor LVEF), hypertension (higher rate in histiocytic neoplasms than melanoma), pyrexia (BRAFi)

doseModificationRules.text: It is generally reasonable to start with one or two dose reductions and then adjust based on response (HIST-F, Considerations for Targeted Therapies). Manage CYP drug-drug interactions.

doseModificationRules.condition: MEK-inhibitor retinopathy or significant LVEF decline
doseModificationRules.text: Hold/reduce the MEK inhibitor per prescribing information; ophthalmology/cardiology evaluation. Obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: lines 23127, 23213 (BRAF V600E present in ~39-50% of Langerhans cell histiocytosis and >80% of BRAF V600E histiocytosis; BRAF-inhibitor response in histiocytosis)

guideline.locator: HIST-F (Principles of Targeted Therapy, Recommended Starting Doses): Dabrafenib 50 mg PO BID (line 2730), Cobimetinib 20-40 mg PO daily days 1-21 q28d (line 2732), Trametinib 0.5-1 mg PO daily (line 2734), Vemurafenib 480 mg PO BID (line 2736); Discussion MS-9 (BRAF/MEK inhibitors for LCH and ECD; V600E gate; MEKi for MAPK-pathway mutation); histiocytic lines 3358, 3428, 3623, 3627, 3631

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for BRAF inhibitor +/- MEK inhibitor targeted therapy in BRAF V600E-mutated histiocytic neoplasm (LCH / Erdheim-Chester disease), a rare histiocytic disorder. All doses are dose-grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Histiocytic Neoplasms v2.2026, HIST-F 'Recommended Starting Doses for Select Targeted Agents': dabrafenib 50 mg PO BID (line 2730), vemurafenib 480 mg PO BID (line 2736, alternative BRAFi), trametinib 0.5-1 mg PO daily (line 2734), cobimetinib 20-40 mg PO daily days 1-21 q28d (line 2732, alternative MEKi). The modeled combination is dabrafenib + trametinib; the alternative BRAFi (vemurafenib) and MEKi (cobimetinib), and BRAFi-monotherapy (omit MEKi), are carried in notes/supportive care - no dose is invented (trametinib modeled at the 1 mg upper end of the source 0.5-1 mg starting range, range noted). BIOMARKER GATE: BRAF V600E is required for BRAF-inhibitor therapy; MEK inhibitors serve MAP-kinase-pathway mutations or no detectable actionable mutation. MEK-inhibitor retinopathy (OCT monitoring) is captured. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
